# Traceability chain for %CAR+ (CAR expression, % of CD3+)

%CAR+ is controlled and tested through the transduction step. The main finding is that vector potency is the weak link. One open deviation blames the donor, but the data point to a degraded vector lot.

## 1. Definition, measurement and validation
- **Attribute:** %CAR+ is CQA #8 in PPQ-001, with a limit of ≥20 % of CD3+. VCN per CAR+ cell (criterion 9, ≤5) is the linked CQA.
- **Method:** AM-FC-CAR (CAR expression by flow cytometry, QC test FC-CAR, SOP-QC-202 v2.0) has status VALIDATED.
  - Validated range is 5–90 % of CD3+, which covers the ≥20 limit.
  - AMV-FC-CAR-01 is a single test case, TC-AMV-CAR-01 (accuracy, precision, range). Execution TX-0086 passed on 2026-03-20 and the report is approved.
- **Reporting:** FC-CAR is reported as RELEASE for PPQ and as RELEASE-INFO for engineering runs. Characterisation results appear as CHAR.

## 2. Process parameters that drive it
| Parameter | PPQ-001 range | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **MOI** (CPP 1) | 4–6 TU/cell | DoE-MOI-01/02/03: %CAR+ averaged about 22 % at MOI 2.5, 39 % at 5, 65 % at 10 and 76 % at 15. VCN rose with it (about 1.6, 2.4, 3.2 and 4.8), so the VCN ≤5 limit caps how far MOI can go. |
| **Vector lot titer and storage** (not a PPQ CPP) | n/a | Vector volume is calculated from the CoA titer (MOI × cells ÷ titer). A degraded lot therefore gives a lower real MOI without any EBR signal. See section 6. |
| **Time from activation to transduction** (CPP 5) | 20–30 h | Weak positive correlation with %CAR+ (r ≈ 0.3). The 18 h batch PD26-032 gave 27.6 % against about 38 % typical. |
| Seeding density (CPP 2), culture duration (CPP 4) | 0.4–0.6 ×10⁶/mL; 7–9 days | No correlation with %CAR+ in the data (seeding r ≈ 0). The pFMEA links them to Tscm and expansion, not %CAR+. |
| Donor CD3 % and apheresis hold time | n/a | No correlation (CD3 r ≈ 0, hold r ≈ 0.2). |

## 3. Risks that threaten it (pFMEA RA-PFMEA-001)
- **Direct, with %CAR+ named as impacted:**
  - **FM-06** (MOI below target) is HIGH, RPN 128. Its stated cause is titer over-estimated or vector degradation. Its controls are the EBR calculation and the CoA titer.
  - **FM-15** (OOS result not flagged) is HIGH, RPN 80. It affects %CAR+, VCN, viability and CD3.
- **Indirect, with transduction efficiency impacted:**
  - **FM-07** (vector held above -70 °C) is HIGH, RPN 96. It lists "Transduction efficiency; VCN" as impacted.
  - **FM-08** (transduction outside 20–30 h) is MEDIUM, RPN 54. Its CQA is recorded only as "TE".
  - **FM-05** (MOI above target) is HIGH, RPN 108. It mainly affects VCN.
- **Not %CAR+:** FM-11 and FM-12 name "CAR+ viable cell dose". That is a dose attribute, not %CAR+.
- **Naming inconsistency:** the CQA is written as "%CAR+", "TE" and "Transduction efficiency", so a search on %CAR+ alone misses FM-07 and FM-08.

## 4. Controls and test evidence, including gaps
| Risk | Mitigating items | Test evidence | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | URS-EBR-007 (vector volume calculation), SOP-MFG-104 | TC-OQ-EBR-04 passed (TX-0083). It tested 2.5–10 TU/cell against an independent calculation. | The calculation is verified, but nothing controls actual vector titer or degradation. |
| FM-05 / FM-06 | URS-EBR-009 (MOI outside 4.0–6.0 rejected, hard stop in CS-EBR-03) | **None.** CS-EBR-03 and URS-EBR-009 have no test case, although FRA-042 rates the requirement HIGH and "SCRIPTED (robust)". | **Gap: untested range-check control.** |
| FM-07 | URS-ULT-001/002, URS-EMS-014, SOP-MAT-401 | ULT OQ/PQ and TC-OQ-EMS-04 all passed. | The ULT checks passed, but the control failed in practice (section 6). |
| FM-08 | SOP-MFG-104 only | None. The control is a "batch record timing check", with no spec or test link. | **Gap** |
| FM-15 | URS-LIMS-003 and URS-LIMS-002, traced via CS-LIMS-01 and CS-LIMS-02 | TC-OQ-LIMS-03 passed (TX-0075, "OOS flagged for all release tests"). TC-OQ-LIMS-02 passed (TX-0074). | None. Coverage is indirect, through the TRACE links. |

The assurance_approach field is blank for every pFMEA item, FM-06 included.

## 5. PPQ performance (PPQ-001, 5 batches)
- All five batches passed the ≥20 % limit:

| Batch | %CAR+ | Vector lot |
|---|---|---|
| PPQ26-01 | 44.6 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-02 | 39.2 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-03 | 36.1 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-04 | 38.9 | LV26-021 |
| PPQ26-05 | 37.3 | LV26-021 |

- VCN stayed between 1.79 and 2.39, well under the ≤5 limit.
- MOI was 5.0 on every batch. Time from activation to transduction was 21.9–23.7 h, inside 20–30 h.
- The PPQ-001 status is "EXECUTION COMPLETE - REPORT PENDING".
- PPQ26-02 failed criterion 6 (harvest viability) because of an incubator door-latch issue (DEV-26-033). That deviation is not a %CAR+ failure.

## 6. Related deviations and what connects them
- **DEV-26-027** (open, MINOR, ATYPICAL_RESULT) covers low %CAR+ in ENG26-01 (19.8 %) and ENG26-02 (11.9 %).
  - Its root cause is "suspected donor variability (low CD3 % at apheresis)".
  - It links to CAPA-26-016 (evaluate a minimum CD3 % at apheresis receipt, open).
  - **The data do not support the donor explanation.** Apheresis CD3 was 65.3 % and 63.8 %, which is higher than PPQ26-04 (50.1 %), a batch that passed with 38.9 % CAR+.
- **Evidence for a vector-lot cause:**
  - FRZ-80-02 failed on 2026-04-20 (DEV-26-021, MAJOR, compressor failure). The chamber warmed from about -67 °C at 04:00 to about -36 °C when contents were moved at 15:30. It stayed above -70 °C for about 11.5 hours. The excursion log shows a peak of -10 °C at 10:00 on 23 April.
  - The alarm started at 03:20 and was acknowledged at 14:40 by warehouse staff, about 11 hours late against the 15-minute escalation requirement (URS-EMS-014).
  - Lot LV25-118 was stored in FRZ-80-02. The other vector lots were in FRZ-80-01.
  - DEV-26-021 concluded "low risk", with no lots held and no titer retest. The CoA titer of 1.04×10⁸ TU/mL stayed in use.
  - %CAR+ with LV25-118 was 35–41 % before the excursion. After it, all seven batches were low: PD26-024, 025, 026 and 027 (14.9–17.3 %) and ENG26-01, 02 and 03 (19.8, 11.9 and 13.9 %). Lots LV26-007 and LV26-021 averaged about 41–44 % at the same MOI.
  - **ENG26-03 (13.9 %) is not covered by DEV-26-027**, and neither are the four PD runs. The deviation is also not linked to DEV-26-021.
  - This is the failure mode named in FM-06 (vector degradation) and FM-07 (vector held above -70 °C). The data are consistent with it but do not prove it, because no potency retest exists.
- **CC-26-011** rebuilt the EMS notification groups (CS-EMS-03) on 2026-03-12 with "no re-testing required". TC-OQ-EMS-04 was last run on 2026-01-20. The late acknowledgement in April is consistent with a possible escalation failure, but I haven't confirmed that cause.
- **CC-26-014** (compressor replacement) re-ran only the pull-down and alarm tests (TX-0091 and TX-0092). It did not address stored vector.
- **CC-26-022** (open, at impact assessment) proposes raising target MOI from 5.0 to 8.0 TU/cell to improve %CAR+.
  - It exceeds the validated 4–6 TU/cell CPP range and the URS-EBR-009 hard stop.
  - Its basis is the DoE data, yet all PPQ batches already pass at MOI 5. The low results coincide with a suspect vector lot, not an MOI problem.
  - At MOI 15 the DoE gave a VCN of up to 4.99, right at the ≤5 limit.
- **Link map:** DEV-26-027 → ENG26-01 / ENG26-02 and CAPA-26-016. DEV-26-021 → FRZ-80-02 → CAPA-26-008 → CC-26-014 → TX-0091 / TX-0092. PPQ-001 → PPQ26-01 to 05, with DEV-26-033 on PPQ26-02. The explicit links from DEV-26-027 to FRZ-80-02, vector lot LV25-118 or DEV-26-021 are missing, and so is the one from DEV-26-021 to FM-07.

## Recommended actions
1. Reopen the root cause of DEV-26-027. Retest the functional titer of LV25-118, and extend the scope to ENG26-03 and PD26-024 to 027.
2. Add a test for URS-EBR-009 (the MOI hard stop).
3. Link FM-08 to a specification and a test.
4. Review whether CC-26-011 needed a retest of escalation.
5. Hold the MOI 8.0 proposal until the vector issue is resolved.

# Traceability chain for %CAR+ (CAR expression, % of CD3+)

%CAR+ is controlled and tested through the transduction step. The main finding is that vector potency is the weak link. One open deviation blames the donor, but the data point to a degraded vector lot.

## 1. Definition, measurement and validation
- **Attribute:** %CAR+ is CQA #8 in PPQ-001, with a limit of ≥20 % of CD3+. VCN per CAR+ cell (criterion 9, ≤5) is the linked CQA.
- **Method:** AM-FC-CAR (CAR expression by flow cytometry, QC test FC-CAR, SOP-QC-202 v2.0) has status VALIDATED.
  - Validated range is 5–90 % of CD3+, which covers the ≥20 limit.
  - AMV-FC-CAR-01 is a single test case, TC-AMV-CAR-01 (accuracy, precision, range). Execution TX-0086 passed on 2026-03-20 and the report is approved.
- **Reporting:** FC-CAR is reported as RELEASE for PPQ and as RELEASE-INFO for engineering runs. Characterisation results appear as CHAR.

## 2. Process parameters that drive it
| Parameter | PPQ-001 range | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **MOI** (CPP 1) | 4–6 TU/cell | DoE-MOI-01/02/03: %CAR+ averaged about 22 % at MOI 2.5, 39 % at 5, 65 % at 10 and 76 % at 15. VCN rose with it (about 1.6, 2.4, 3.2 and 4.8), so the VCN ≤5 limit caps how far MOI can go. |
| **Vector lot titer and storage** (not a PPQ CPP) | n/a | Vector volume is calculated from the CoA titer (MOI × cells ÷ titer). A degraded lot therefore gives a lower real MOI without any EBR signal. See section 6. |
| **Time from activation to transduction** (CPP 5) | 20–30 h | Weak positive correlation with %CAR+ (r ≈ 0.3). The 18 h batch PD26-032 gave 27.6 % against about 38 % typical. |
| Seeding density (CPP 2), culture duration (CPP 4) | 0.4–0.6 ×10⁶/mL; 7–9 days | No correlation with %CAR+ in the data (seeding r ≈ 0). The pFMEA links them to Tscm and expansion, not %CAR+. |
| Donor CD3 % and apheresis hold time | n/a | No correlation (CD3 r ≈ 0, hold r ≈ 0.2). |

## 3. Risks that threaten it (pFMEA RA-PFMEA-001)
- **Direct, with %CAR+ named as impacted:**
  - **FM-06** (MOI below target) is HIGH, RPN 128. Its stated cause is titer over-estimated or vector degradation. Its controls are the EBR calculation and the CoA titer.
  - **FM-15** (OOS result not flagged) is HIGH, RPN 80. It affects %CAR+, VCN, viability and CD3.
- **Indirect, with transduction efficiency impacted:**
  - **FM-07** (vector held above -70 °C) is HIGH, RPN 96. It lists "Transduction efficiency; VCN" as impacted.
  - **FM-08** (transduction outside 20–30 h) is MEDIUM, RPN 54. Its CQA is recorded only as "TE".
  - **FM-05** (MOI above target) is HIGH, RPN 108. It mainly affects VCN.
- **Not %CAR+:** FM-11 and FM-12 name "CAR+ viable cell dose". That is a dose attribute, not %CAR+.
- **Naming inconsistency:** the CQA is written as "%CAR+", "TE" and "Transduction efficiency", so a search on %CAR+ alone misses FM-07 and FM-08.

## 4. Controls and test evidence, including gaps
| Risk | Mitigating items | Test evidence | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | URS-EBR-007 (vector volume calculation), SOP-MFG-104 | TC-OQ-EBR-04 passed (TX-0083). It tested 2.5–10 TU/cell against an independent calculation. | The calculation is verified, but nothing controls actual vector titer or degradation. |
| FM-05 / FM-06 | URS-EBR-009 (MOI outside 4.0–6.0 rejected, hard stop in CS-EBR-03) | **None.** CS-EBR-03 and URS-EBR-009 have no test case, although FRA-042 rates the requirement HIGH and "SCRIPTED (robust)". | **Gap: untested range-check control.** |
| FM-07 | URS-ULT-001/002, URS-EMS-014, SOP-MAT-401 | ULT OQ/PQ and TC-OQ-EMS-04 all passed. | The ULT checks passed, but the control failed in practice (section 6). |
| FM-08 | SOP-MFG-104 only | None. The control is a "batch record timing check", with no spec or test link. | **Gap** |
| FM-15 | URS-LIMS-003 and URS-LIMS-002, traced via CS-LIMS-01 and CS-LIMS-02 | TC-OQ-LIMS-03 passed (TX-0075, "OOS flagged for all release tests"). TC-OQ-LIMS-02 passed (TX-0074). | None. Coverage is indirect, through the TRACE links. |

The assurance_approach field is blank for every pFMEA item, FM-06 included.

## 5. PPQ performance (PPQ-001, 5 batches)
- All five batches passed the ≥20 % limit:

| Batch | %CAR+ | Vector lot |
|---|---|---|
| PPQ26-01 | 44.6 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-02 | 39.2 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-03 | 36.1 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-04 | 38.9 | LV26-021 |
| PPQ26-05 | 37.3 | LV26-021 |

- VCN stayed between 1.79 and 2.39, well under the ≤5 limit.
- MOI was 5.0 on every batch. Time from activation to transduction was 21.9–23.7 h, inside 20–30 h.
- The PPQ-001 status is "EXECUTION COMPLETE - REPORT PENDING".
- PPQ26-02 failed criterion 6 (harvest viability) because of an incubator door-latch issue (DEV-26-033). That deviation is not a %CAR+ failure.

## 6. Related deviations and what connects them
- **DEV-26-027** (open, MINOR, ATYPICAL_RESULT) covers low %CAR+ in ENG26-01 (19.8 %) and ENG26-02 (11.9 %).
  - Its root cause is "suspected donor variability (low CD3 % at apheresis)".
  - It links to CAPA-26-016 (evaluate a minimum CD3 % at apheresis receipt, open).
  - **The data do not support the donor explanation.** Apheresis CD3 was 65.3 % and 63.8 %, which is higher than PPQ26-04 (50.1 %), a batch that passed with 38.9 % CAR+.
- **Evidence for a vector-lot cause:**
  - FRZ-80-02 failed on 2026-04-20 (DEV-26-021, MAJOR, compressor failure). The chamber warmed from about -67 °C at 04:00 to about -36 °C when contents were moved at 15:30. It stayed above -70 °C for about 11.5 hours. The excursion log shows a peak of -10 °C at 10:00 on 23 April.
  - The alarm started at 03:20 and was acknowledged at 14:40 by warehouse staff, about 11 hours late against the 15-minute escalation requirement (URS-EMS-014).
  - Lot LV25-118 was stored in FRZ-80-02. The other vector lots were in FRZ-80-01.
  - DEV-26-021 concluded "low risk", with no lots held and no titer retest. The CoA titer of 1.04×10⁸ TU/mL stayed in use.
  - %CAR+ with LV25-118 was 35–41 % before the excursion. After it, all seven batches were low: PD26-024, 025, 026 and 027 (14.9–17.3 %) and ENG26-01, 02 and 03 (19.8, 11.9 and 13.9 %). Lots LV26-007 and LV26-021 averaged about 41–44 % at the same MOI.
  - **ENG26-03 (13.9 %) is not covered by DEV-26-027**, and neither are the four PD runs. The deviation is also not linked to DEV-26-021.
  - This is the failure mode named in FM-06 (vector degradation) and FM-07 (vector held above -70 °C). The data are consistent with it but do not prove it, because no potency retest exists.
- **CC-26-011** rebuilt the EMS notification groups (CS-EMS-03) on 2026-03-12 with "no re-testing required". TC-OQ-EMS-04 was last run on 2026-01-20. The late acknowledgement in April is consistent with a possible escalation failure, but I haven't confirmed that cause.
- **CC-26-014** (compressor replacement) re-ran only the pull-down and alarm tests (TX-0091 and TX-0092). It did not address stored vector.
- **CC-26-022** (open, at impact assessment) proposes raising target MOI from 5.0 to 8.0 TU/cell to improve %CAR+.
  - It exceeds the validated 4–6 TU/cell CPP range and the URS-EBR-009 hard stop.
  - Its basis is the DoE data, yet all PPQ batches already pass at MOI 5. The low results coincide with a suspect vector lot, not an MOI problem.
  - At MOI 15 the DoE gave a VCN of up to 4.99, right at the ≤5 limit.
- **Link map:** DEV-26-027 → ENG26-01 / ENG26-02 and CAPA-26-016. DEV-26-021 → FRZ-80-02 → CAPA-26-008 → CC-26-014 → TX-0091 / TX-0092. PPQ-001 → PPQ26-01 to 05, with DEV-26-033 on PPQ26-02. The explicit links from DEV-26-027 to FRZ-80-02, vector lot LV25-118 or DEV-26-021 are missing, and so is the one from DEV-26-021 to FM-07.

## Recommended actions
1. Reopen the root cause of DEV-26-027. Retest the functional titer of LV25-118, and extend the scope to ENG26-03 and PD26-024 to 027.
2. Add a test for URS-EBR-009 (the MOI hard stop).
3. Link FM-08 to a specification and a test.
4. Review whether CC-26-011 needed a retest of escalation.
5. Hold the MOI 8.0 proposal until the vector issue is resolved.
